title: A small deck for two-dimensional vectors
subtitle: Practice the dot product through definitions, distinctions, and a worked example.

lecture.title: Original VMF demonstration mini-lesson; no indexed video

gaps: This is an original redistribution-safe example, not a transcript or a live VMF retrieval.

sources.summary: For real two-dimensional vectors u=(a,b) and v=(c,d), define u·v=ac+bd. The result is a scalar.
The dot product of a vector with itself is the sum of its squared coordinates, so it is nonnegative. For nonzero real vectors, a zero dot product indicates perpendicular directions.
Scaling one vector by a real factor k scales its dot product by k: (ku)·v=k(u·v).

cards.front: What is the dot product of real vectors (a, b) and (c, d)?
cards.back: ac + bd: multiply matching coordinates, then add.
cards.hint: Pair first coordinates and second coordinates.
cards.rationale: This restates the definition in the original synthetic mini-lesson.

cards.front: Is the dot product of two vectors itself a vector?
cards.back: No. The dot product is a scalar, even though its inputs are vectors.
cards.rationale: The coordinate definition adds real products and therefore returns one real number.

cards.front: Can a real vector have a negative dot product with itself?
cards.back: No. It is a sum of squares, so it is nonnegative.
cards.rationale: a²+b² is at least zero for real a and b; it is zero only for the zero vector.

cards.hint: Include the sign of the second product.
cards.rationale: Apply the real coordinate definition term by term; the minus sign belongs to −1.

cards.front: If u · v = 2, what is (3u) · v?
cards.back: 6. Scaling one input by 3 scales the dot product by 3.

cards.front: For two nonzero real vectors, what does a zero dot product imply about their directions?
cards.back: They are perpendicular. The nonzero condition avoids assigning a direction to the zero vector.
cards.rationale: The synthetic lesson states the perpendicularity criterion for nonzero inputs; the question preserves that condition.
